title: Isomorphisms, Cayley's theorem and direct products
summary: Isomorphisms as structure-preserving bijections and the invariants they preserve; classification of cyclic groups (infinite cyclic groups are isomorphic to Z, cyclic groups of order n to Z_n); isomorphism as an equivalence relation; Cayley's theorem; external and internal direct products and when Z_m × Z_n is cyclic.

objectives.description: Objectives for this unit will be finalised when it is prepared; the source material is chapter 9 of Judson (Sections 9.1–9.2).

preparation.description: Read Section 9.1: definition and examples, Theorem 9.1.6 (invariants), Theorems 9.1.7–9.1.8 and Corollary 9.1.9 (classification of cyclic groups), Theorem 9.1.10, Cayley's theorem (Theorem 9.1.12).
Read Section 9.2 (external and internal direct products) from the chapter page.
Optional supplement: MIT student notes, lecture 3 (Homomorphisms and Isomorphisms).
